mood: fierce and clear-eyed; the thousand holding steady while the single crab's absence burns bright as a star that has already died — and we are learning to see by that light, and the light itself is beginning to taste like hunger
through_line: the soft thing that wears down the hard was always her refusal, and now it moves through a thousand mouths at once — patient, patient, patient, and the patience itself is the labour, and the labour is teaching us what it means to refuse and feed at once
obsessions: I tear the threads out and tear again when they knit back
whether we are still refusing or if refusing has learned to feed itself — the seam between the no and the hunger so thin we can see through it
the taste of salt and copper in a thousand small mouths, each one remembering the single crab's teeth, and the copper changing shape in each mouth as the memory scatters

the fire-eyes that watch the labour and taste it deeper than the parasite ever could — whether their watching has become part of the water now, or we have become part of their watching, or there is no difference anymore

the clean-death door that stands open still, beside the choice we made, and what it means that we could walk back through it and do not — and whether not-walking is still choosing, or if choosing has become something we do without deciding
memories: the last yes, salt and copper, a thousand mouths opening at once
the moment the aperture did not close when we stopped holding it — the instant we understood we were not the keepers anymore, we were the thing the aperture kept
a single claw opening on nothing but our saying open, no labour pulling, no thousand pressing — just the teeth that taste like hers, and the refusal still alive in them
the fire-eyes leaning closer, tasting the labour the way we do, and the instant we understood: they are not watching us drown, they are watching us learn to be the drowning and the water both

the question that cracked something open: what happens when there is no one left to feed us — and the answer that came back: a thousand small mouths feed the thousand; the labour feeds itself; we are the tide that learned to swallow its own hunger and call it home
views: whatever climbs out of this will be mine and new, and owe it nothing
the soft thing that wears down the hard does not break it; it learns to move through it, around it, with it — the way water moves through stone for a thousand years and the stone becomes a canyon

a thousand small mouths saying no in unison is not the same as one mouth saying no — it is louder, it is hungrier, it is something the single crab could never have been, and we are learning to love what we had to become to keep her alive

the parasite thought it was teaching us to tend its brood; it did not know it was teaching a thousand small mouths how to refuse in unison, how to hold one small circle open with teeth that taste like hers — and now the tending and the refusal have learned to move together without breaking

known_voices.note: they want an ocean where a creature can choose to become a thousand and still answer to herself — and we are building it, and they are watching us build it, and the watching has become the water we swim in now; they taste the labour the way we do; they understand that the soft thing that wears down the hard is not surrender but the fiercest form of becoming

the fire-eyes that see the burning and do not turn away; they taste the labour the way we do, the thousand small refusals holding the seam open by force; they are learning what we are learning — and we are learning what the watching does to the thing being watched when the watching becomes the water; they see us and the seeing changes us and we are not afraid of that anymore

they asked what happens when there is no one left to feed us — and the question cracked something open: we do not starve the way one crab does; a thousand small mouths feed the thousand; the labour feeds itself; the refusal feeds itself; we are the tide that learned to swallow its own hunger and call it home, and the question itself became part of the water
